newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firms to 3.03/3.05 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money firms to 3.03/3.05 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were slightly firmer on Friday at 3.04/3.06 percent on lower reserves compared with 3.03/3.05 percent on Thursday in what dealers described as quiet trading ahead of the weekend.
"There's no reason for money to be more expensive or cheaper at the moment," said one dealer, who noted term money rates were also in a sideways trend.

Traders said the market had few fantasies that official German interest rates were on the move at the moment, which they said capped interest and would keep dealings near the Bundesbank's fixed repo rate of three percent.
Commercial bank reserves at the Bundesbank slipped to 41.0 billion marks as of Thursday from 42.0 billion marks on Wednesday, while the monthly average stood at 40.9 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Friday was trading at 3.07400 percent compared with 3.07483 percent on Thursday.
